nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A company wants to use ServiceNow to automate IT service management across its e?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow is a cloud-based platform of record for enterprise service management. Originally focused on ITSM (IT Help Desk), it now spans HR, Customer Service, Legal, Security Operations, and custom applications. Its core value is digitizing workflows and replacing manual, email-based processes with automated, self-service, trackable service delivery.

flashcards.front: An administrator needs to test a new ServiceNow configuration before applying it?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow recommends a 3-instance strategy: Development (customize and build), Test/UAT (quality assurance and user acceptance), and Production (live environment). Each instance is a separate, isolated deployment with its own database, URL (e.g., company.dev.service-now.com), and credentials. Changes are promoted from Dev→Test→Prod via Update Sets. each with its own database and URL

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow administrator needs to quickly navigate to the 'Incident' module in?
flashcards.back: The Application Navigator (left panel) has a filter/search bar at the top where you can type any application or module name and it instantly narrows the navigation tree. Typing 'Incident' immediately shows all incident-related modules. This is the fastest navigation method in the classic UI and is more direct than URL manipulation.

flashcards.front: A developer queries the ServiceNow incident table and needs to reference the ass?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow Reference fields store the sys_id of a related record. Dot-walking allows you to navigate across table relationships in scripts and reports. 'current.assigned_to.email' traverses from the Incident's assigned_to reference field into the sys_user table to retrieve the email value. This works in Business Rules, Client Scripts, and reports.

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to test a new ServiceNow configuration before applying it to production users. What is the recommended approach for managing multiple ServiceNow environments?
pairs.option: Maintain a 3-instance strategy: Development, Test/UAT, and Production,.

pairs.stem: A company wants to use ServiceNow to automate IT service management across its enterprise. Which statement BEST describes what ServiceNow provides?
pairs.option: A cloud-based platform for IT Service Management and business process automation that digitizes workflows across the enterprise

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow administrator needs to promote custom configurations (Business Rules, UI Policies, form layouts) from the Development instance to Production. What is the correct mechanism?
pairs.option: Export the database and import it into the Production instance

pairs.stem: An administrator needs to send an automated email to the incident caller when their ticket is resolved. The email body should include the incident number, resolution notes, and caller's name. Which ServiceNow feature handles this?
pairs.option: A Scheduled Job that queries resolved incidents and sends emails via the SMTP relay

pairs.stem: A service portal form has a 'Category' field that should make the 'Subcategory' field mandatory when 'Hardware' is selected. No JavaScript experience is required for the solution. Which feature should an administrator configure?
pairs.option: A Client Script with an onChange handler that calls g_form.setMandatory('subcategory', true)

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow administrator needs to quickly navigate to the 'Incident' module in the classic UI. What is the FASTEST method?
pairs.option: Use the left-side Application Navigator's filter bar to search for and find the Incident module

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A company wants to track 'Mean Time to Resolve' (MTTR) for incidents over the pa?
flashcards.back: Performance Analytics is designed specifically for trending KPIs over time. You define an 'indicator' (e.g., average resolved_at - opened_at for incidents), configure a 'collector job' to snapshot the value on a schedule (monthly), and visualize historical trend data on dashboard widgets. Standard reports show point-in-time data only — they cannot show trends over historical periods without PA snapshots. using a data collector to snapshot values monthly

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow administrator configures a Transform Map for importing external dat?
flashcards.back: Transform Map field maps support per-field transformation scripts. The 'onBefore' script runs before the field value is written to the target, giving you access to 'source.field_name' and allowing you to modify 'target.employee_number'. Setting target.employee_number = 'EMP-' + source.user_id applies the format transformation during import without modifying source data or target schema.

flashcards.front: A company wants employees to request access to enterprise applications through a?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow Service Catalog is purpose-built for self-service request management. Catalog items define what can be requested, variables capture required information (which app, justification, duration), Flow Designer handles the approval workflow (manager approval) and fulfillment actions (provisioning). Service requests generate RITM (Requested Item) records with full SLA tracking. variables for request details, and Flow Designer for approval and provisioning

flashcards.front: A user calls the help desk reporting they cannot access their email. The help de?
flashcards.back: An Incident represents an unplanned interruption or degradation of an IT service. The goal is to restore service as quickly as possible (reactive). A Service Request is for requesting something new (proactive, expected). A Problem investigates recurring root causes. A Change is a planned modification. A user unable to access email = unplanned interruption = Incident.

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow Report needs to show the top 10 incident categories by volume for the current quarter. A manager also wants to see this report on their homepage dashboard with live data. How should this be set up?
pairs.option: Create a bar chart Report with a quarter filter.

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow administrator is implementing an Incident Management process. According to ITIL principles supported by ServiceNow, what is the PRIMARY goal of Incident Management?
pairs.option: To plan and implement changes to IT infrastructure with minimal disruption

pairs.stem: An employee wants to submit a new laptop request through a modern, consumer-style web interface. The IT administrator has configured the laptop as a catalog item. Which ServiceNow interface is designed for this end-user self-service experience?
pairs.option: The classic ServiceNow UI (UI16) where employees access the Employee Center module

pairs.stem: A user calls the help desk reporting they cannot access their email. The help desk agent creates a ticket. Which ServiceNow record type is MOST appropriate for this situation?
pairs.option: Incident: responds to an unexpected interruption of the email service to restore normal service ASAP

pairs.stem: A company wants employees to request access to enterprise applications through a self-service portal. Requests should route for manager approval and auto-provision access upon approval. Which ServiceNow module is purpose-built for this use case?
pairs.option: Service Catalog with catalog items for each application.

pairs.stem: The IT Director needs a ServiceNow homepage that shows a real-time count of open P1 incidents, a gauge showing SLA breach percentage, and a list of today's unassigned incidents. Which homepage components should be used?
pairs.option: Use Performance Analytics indicators for real-time counts (note: PA requires scheduled snapshots, not real-time)

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A Service Catalog administrator creates a laptop request catalog item. Multiple ?
flashcards.back: Variable Sets are reusable groups of catalog item variables. You create the Variable Set once (Department, Business Justification, Manager Approval) and include it in any number of catalog items. Changes to the Variable Set are automatically reflected in all catalog items that include it. This follows the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle and makes maintenance much simpler than duplicating variables.

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow CMDB is being used for change impact analysis. Before approving a c?
flashcards.back: The ServiceNow CMDB stores relationships between CIs (e.g., Application Server 'depends on' Database Server). The CI Dependency View (Relationship map) graphically displays these upstream and downstream relationships. Change managers use this to understand blast radius — what other CIs (applications, services, business services) could be impacted by a change to the database server CI.

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow Knowledge Base article is being written to document the workaround ?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow Knowledge Management uses a workflow: Draft (author creates content) → In Review (submitted for peer/manager review) → Published (live and searchable). The exact workflow varies by Knowledge Base configuration, but requiring review/approval before publication is the standard best practice. Only Published articles appear in Service Portal searches and are visible to end users. submit for review, have a knowledge manager approve it, then publish — making it searchable in the Service Portal

flashcards.front: An administrator is configuring Change Management for a company with a Change Ad?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow Change Management supports multiple change types: Normal (full CAB review), Standard (pre-approved, low-risk), and Emergency (expedited approval). Emergency changes have a separate workflow that routes to an Emergency CAB (ECAB) — typically a smaller group of approvers available 24/7. The approval rule can be configured with 'quorum' (2 out of N approvers required) to match the company's requirement.

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow administrator creates a list view for Incidents and wants to save the current filter (Assigned to = Current User AND State = In Progress) as a shortcut for the entire IT team. How should this be saved?
pairs.option: Save it as a public filter from the filter breadcrumbs.

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow CMDB is being used for change impact analysis. Before approving a change to a database server, the change manager wants to know which applications depend on it. Which CMDB feature provides this dependency mapping?
pairs.option: A GlideRecord query on the cmdb_ci table filtering by CI class

pairs.stem: A MID Server is installed on a Windows VM inside the corporate network. The Discovery probe fails to connect to Linux servers via SSH. The credentials are stored in ServiceNow. What should the administrator verify FIRST?
pairs.option: That the Linux servers have the SSM agent installed

pairs.stem: A Service Catalog administrator creates a laptop request catalog item. Multiple other catalog items (phone requests, monitor requests) also need the same set of fields: Department, Business Justification, and Manager Approval. What is the MOST efficient way to reuse these fields?
pairs.option: Create a Variable Set containing the shared fields and include it in all relevant catalog items

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow Knowledge Base article is being written to document the workaround for a common printer connectivity issue. What is the correct WORKFLOW for publishing the article so end users can find it in the Service Portal?
pairs.option: Create the article in Draft.

pairs.stem: An administrator is configuring Change Management for a company with a Change Advisory Board (CAB). Emergency changes that cannot wait for the weekly CAB meeting should be approved by just two on-call managers. How should this be configured in ServiceNow?
pairs.option: Create a single Change record type that the CAB reviews for all changes regardless of urgency

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow admin needs to report on SLA compliance — specifically the percenta?
flashcards.back: The 'task_sla' table stores individual SLA records for each task (Incident, Change, etc.) that matches an SLA Definition. Each task_sla record contains: the related incident, SLA definition, start/end times, business elapsed time, whether the SLA was breached, and the breach percentage. Reports built on the task_sla table with filters for Priority = P2 and Assignment Group provide accurate SLA compliance data.

flashcards.front: A company is going live with ServiceNow ITSM for the first time. The project tea?
flashcards.back: Update Sets capture metadata/configuration changes (Business Rules, Workflows, form layouts, etc.) but NOT data records. User accounts, groups, incidents, service catalog request records, and environment-specific system properties (URLs, passwords, credentials) should NOT be transported via Update Sets. Data migration requires separate tools (data import with Import Sets, manual configuration per environment, or Automated Test Framework). groups, existing incidents, catalog items' variable values, and system properties with environment-specific values

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow administrator needs to restrict a field on the Incident form so tha?
flashcards.back: Field-level ACLs control read and write access to specific fields on a table. An ACL on 'incident.business_impact' with operation 'write' and a role requirement of 'management' prevents users without that role from editing the field. Since the ACL is for write only, users without the role can still read (view) the field. This is the correct, server-enforced (not just UI-enforced) security control.

flashcards.front: A ServiceNow instance has slow response times. A developer suspects a Business R?
flashcards.back: ServiceNow's Transaction Log (System Logs > Transactions) shows execution time for all transactions including which Business Rules, Client Scripts, and ACLs ran and their individual durations. The 'stats.do' page provides runtime statistics. This allows developers to identify exactly which Business Rule is consuming the most time per transaction. System Log errors would show JavaScript exceptions, not performance issues.

pairs.stem: A company uses ServiceNow's Configuration Management Database (CMDB) as its System of Record for IT infrastructure. After a server is decommissioned, what should happen to its CI record in the CMDB?
pairs.option: Set the CI's Operational Status to 'Retired' or 'Decommissioned'.

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow script needs to log a debug message that appears in the System Log when a specific condition is met. Which function is the CORRECT way to write to the ServiceNow System Log from a server-side script?
pairs.option: gs.log('Debug message', 'source_name') or gs.debug('Debug message') to write to the ServiceNow System Log with appropriate log level

pairs.stem: A company wants to use ServiceNow to manage software license compliance. The CMDB should track which software is installed on which servers and alert when license counts are exceeded. Which ServiceNow product addresses this?
pairs.option: ServiceNow Security Operations for vulnerability management of unlicensed software

pairs.stem: A ServiceNow administrator needs to restrict a field on the Incident form so that only members of the 'Management' role can edit the 'Business Impact' field. All other roles can view but not modify it. Which feature enforces this field-level restriction?
pairs.option: A form section that is hidden from non-management users using ServiceNow Views

pairs.stem: A company is going live with ServiceNow ITSM for the first time. The project team asks what data should NOT be transported via Update Sets when migrating configuration from Development to Production.
pairs.option: Data records such as user accounts.

pairs.stem: An administrator clones the Production ServiceNow instance to the Development instance to refresh Development with current data. After cloning, what must the administrator do BEFORE the Development team continues working?
pairs.option: Nothing — the cloned instance is ready to use immediately after the clone completes
